questions.q: Why does a data quality check remain necessary even after a staging table is properly incremental and deduplicated?
options: Those steps don't guarantee the result is trustworthy — rows can still be missing, relationships broken, or nulls present unexpectedly
Incremental loading and deduplication automatically guarantee perfect data quality
Data quality checks are only needed for permanent tables, not staging tables
Deduplication removes the need for any further checks entirely
questions.explain: Correct mechanics (incremental loading, deduplication) don't guarantee correct content — data quality checks catch problems those steps don't address.

questions.q: How does this lesson catch a foreign key that points to a row that doesn't exist (an orphan)?
options: An anti-join — a LEFT JOIN filtered WHERE the joined column IS NULL
A CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE statement
The QUALIFY clause
A COPY INTO statement with validation mode
questions.explain: The anti-join pattern (LEFT JOIN plus a WHERE ... IS NULL filter on the joined side) surfaces rows whose foreign key has no match in the referenced table.

questions.q: Why is a silently dropped row during a load especially hard to notice?
options: The pipeline doesn't error — it just succeeds with fewer rows than it should have
Snowflake always throws a visible error when any row is dropped
Dropped rows are impossible in Snowflake by design
Row-count checks are disabled by default in Snowflake
questions.explain: Nothing fails outright when rows are silently dropped — the load reports success, which is exactly why comparing row counts across layers matters.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does dbt (a later course in this catalog) do relative to the checks taught here?
options: It formalizes the same kinds of checks as declarative config that runs automatically — it doesn't invent a new kind of check
It replaces SQL entirely with a different query language
It performs checks unrelated to nulls, referential integrity, or row counts
It is required before any of these checks can be written
questions.explain: dbt automates running checks like the null, referential, and row-count checks covered here — the underlying logic is the same, just made declarative and automatic.

questions.q: What are the three categories of data quality checks this lesson covers?
options: Completeness (nulls), referential integrity (orphans), and row-count sanity checks between layers
Security, performance, and cost checks
Syntax checks, formatting checks, and naming convention checks
Backup checks, replication checks, and failover checks
questions.explain: The lesson walks through null/completeness checks, referential anti-join checks for orphaned foreign keys, and row-count comparisons between pipeline layers.
